deployment.create.long: Create a remotely managed Deployment. Complex configuration fields accept a JSON value, @file, or - for stdin.
examples:
Example - Scale to zero after five idle minutes:
  agr deployment create \
    --deployment-name workspace-service \
    --tool-id sdt-a1b2c3d4 \
    --scaling-configuration '{"MinInstanceCount":0,"MaxInstanceCount":10,"MaxInstanceRequestConcurrency":100}' \
    --lifecycle-configuration '{"IdleTimeoutSeconds":300,"IdleAction":"STOP"}'

Example - Keep two instances active:
  agr deployment create \
    --deployment-name latency-sensitive-service \
    --tool-id sdt-a1b2c3d4 \
    --scaling-configuration '{"MinInstanceCount":2,"MaxInstanceCount":20,"MaxInstanceRequestConcurrency":200}'

Example - Prefer the same instance for requests sharing an affinity ID:
  agr deployment create \
    --deployment-name session-service \
    --tool-id sdt-a1b2c3d4 \
    --affinity-configuration '{"Mode":"BEST_EFFORT","HeaderName":"X-Tencent-Agr-Affinity-Id"}'

Example - Fail instead of selecting another instance for an affinity ID:
  agr deployment create \
    --deployment-name strict-session-service \
    --tool-id sdt-a1b2c3d4 \
    --affinity-configuration '{"Mode":"STRICT","HeaderName":"X-Tencent-Agr-Affinity-Id"}'

Example - Give each affinity ID an exclusive, non-migrating instance:
  agr deployment create \
    --deployment-name exclusive-session-service \
    --tool-id sdt-a1b2c3d4 \
    --affinity-configuration '{"Mode":"EXCLUSIVE","HeaderName":"X-Tencent-Agr-Affinity-Id"}'

Example - Load configuration from files and capture the Deployment ID:
  deployment_id=$(agr deployment create \
    --deployment-name workspace-service \
    --tool-id sdt-a1b2c3d4 \
    --scaling-configuration @scaling.json \
    --lifecycle-configuration @lifecycle.json \
    --tags @tags.json \
    -o json --jq '.Data.Deployment.DeploymentId')

scaling-configuration.usage: Scaling configuration JSON object, @file, or - for stdin. The object and individual fields are optional; omitted fields use service defaults.
fields: MinInstanceCount: minimum number of active Sandbox Instances; >= 0; default: 0
MaxInstanceCount: maximum number of active Sandbox Instances; >= 1 and >= MinInstanceCount; default: 10
MaxInstanceRequestConcurrency: maximum concurrent Deployment request or connection leases per active Sandbox Instance; >= 1; default: 100

lifecycle-configuration.usage: Idle lifecycle configuration JSON object, @file, or - for stdin. The object and individual fields are optional; omitted fields use service defaults.
fields: IdleTimeoutSeconds: idle seconds after the last active Deployment request or connection before IdleAction; >= 30 with no fixed upper limit; default: 300
IdleAction: STOP releases the Sandbox Instance; PAUSE preserves its state; default: STOP

affinity-configuration.usage: Session affinity configuration JSON object, @file, or - for stdin. Affinity is disabled by default.
fields:
Mode: affinity behavior
  - BEST_EFFORT: prefer the previous Sandbox Instance; select another one when unavailable
  - STRICT: require the previous Sandbox Instance; fail instead of selecting another one
  - EXCLUSIVE: dedicate one non-migrating Sandbox Instance to each affinity ID
  - Empty or omitted: disable affinity

HeaderName: request and response header carrying the affinity ID
  - Default when Mode is enabled: X-Tencent-Agr-Affinity-Id
  - Constraint: a non-reserved HTTP field name of 1-128 ASCII bytes; omit when affinity is disabled

tags.usage: Resource tags as a JSON array, @file, or - for stdin. Omit for no tags.
fields: Key: tag key
Value: tag value

deployment.delete.long: Delete a remotely managed Deployment. By default, return after the delete request is accepted. Use --wait to poll until deletion completes or fails.
examples:
Example - Request deletion and return immediately:
  agr deployment delete dpl-a1b2c3d4

Example - Wait until deletion completes or fails:
  agr deployment delete dpl-a1b2c3d4 --wait

Example - Inspect the Deployment in a human-readable form:
  agr deployment get dpl-a1b2c3d4

Example - Print the complete API response:
  agr deployment get dpl-a1b2c3d4 -o json

Example - Extract the current status for a script:
  agr deployment get dpl-a1b2c3d4 -o json --jq '.Data.Deployment.Status'

Example - List Deployments with compact status and capacity summaries:
  agr deployment list

Example - List active Deployments for one Sandbox Tool:
  agr deployment list --filters '[{"Name":"tool-id","Values":["sdt-a1b2c3d4"]},{"Name":"status","Values":["ACTIVE"]}]'

Example - Find Deployment names containing workspace:
  agr deployment list --filters '[{"Name":"deployment-name-like","Values":["workspace"]}]'

Example - Find Deployments whose last deletion failed:
  agr deployment list --filters '[{"Name":"status","Values":["DELETE_FAILED"]}]'

Example - Read the next page of Deployment IDs:
  agr deployment list --offset 50 --limit 50 -o json --jq '(.Data.DeploymentSet // [])[].DeploymentId'

filters.usage: Filters JSON array, @file, or - for stdin. Names and values are case-sensitive; different filters use AND, while Values within one filter use OR.
values: deployment-name-like: literal substring of the Deployment name; % and _ are not wildcards
status: exact status; ACTIVE, DELETING, or DELETE_FAILED

limit.usage: Maximum number of Deployments to return. Defaults to 20; allowed range: 1-200.

offset.usage: Number of matching Deployments to skip. Defaults to 0; must be non-negative.

deployment.update.long: Update the mutable configuration of a remotely managed Deployment. Provided configuration objects replace their current values in full.
examples:
Example - Increase active capacity:
  agr deployment update dpl-a1b2c3d4 \
    --scaling-configuration '{"MinInstanceCount":2,"MaxInstanceCount":20,"MaxInstanceRequestConcurrency":200}'

Example - Pause idle instances after ten minutes and retain their state:
  agr deployment update dpl-a1b2c3d4 \
    --lifecycle-configuration '{"IdleTimeoutSeconds":600,"IdleAction":"PAUSE"}'

Example - Stop idle instances after five minutes:
  agr deployment update dpl-a1b2c3d4 \
    --lifecycle-configuration '{"IdleTimeoutSeconds":300,"IdleAction":"STOP"}'

Example - Replace all tags:
  agr deployment update dpl-a1b2c3d4 \
    --tags '[{"Key":"env","Value":"production"},{"Key":"team","Value":"agent-platform"}]'

Example - Clear all tags:
  agr deployment update dpl-a1b2c3d4 --tags '[]'

scaling-configuration.usage: Complete scaling configuration JSON object, @file, or - for stdin. Providing it replaces the current scaling configuration; include all three fields because update does not apply create defaults.
fields: MinInstanceCount: minimum number of active Sandbox Instances; >= 0
MaxInstanceCount: maximum number of active Sandbox Instances; >= 1 and >= MinInstanceCount
MaxInstanceRequestConcurrency: maximum concurrent Deployment request or connection leases per active Sandbox Instance; >= 1

lifecycle-configuration.usage: Complete idle lifecycle configuration JSON object, @file, or - for stdin. Providing it replaces the current lifecycle configuration; include both fields because update does not apply create defaults.
fields: IdleTimeoutSeconds: idle seconds after the last active Deployment request or connection before IdleAction; >= 30 with no fixed upper limit
IdleAction: STOP releases the Sandbox Instance; PAUSE preserves its state

tags.usage: Resource tags as a JSON array, @file, or - for stdin. Providing --tags replaces all tags; [] clears all tags; omit --tags to leave tags unchanged.
fields: Key: tag key
Value: tag value

instance.create.long:
Create a new sandbox instance from a tool template, clone an existing instance, or restore a saved snapshot.

To create an instance from a tool, the tool must already exist. Create one first with `agr tool create`, or pass an existing --tool-id.

Use --tool-name/-t for tool name or --tool-id for tool ID.

To clone an existing instance, use --source-instance-id. The source must have disk snapshot support enabled. Instances without this capability cannot be cloned. The new instance inherits the source tool, so a tool selector is optional. If supplied, it must match the source tool. Cloning copies the source system disk into a separate new instance without preserving running processes or memory state. SourceInstanceId is an instance ID, not a saved snapshot ID.

To restore a saved disk-only snapshot into a new instance, use --snapshot-id. The snapshot must be ACTIVE. Restoration uses the tool configuration saved in the snapshot. Do not supply --tool-id or --tool-name/-t with --snapshot-id. Running processes and memory state are not restored. --snapshot-id conflicts with --source-instance-id, --tool-id, and --tool-name/-t. In --request, SnapshotId cannot be combined with SourceInstanceId, ToolId, or ToolName. The Runtime Snapshot API is Beta and may change incompatibly or be discontinued.

Complex API fields such as --mount-options, --metadata, and --custom-configuration accept JSON, @file, or - for stdin.

Auth mode (--auth-mode):
  DEFAULT  Use backend default (currently TOKEN)
  TOKEN    All ports require X-Access-Token
  PUBLIC   envd management port (49983) requires token; other ports open
  NONE     No authentication on any port

timeout.usage: Instance timeout as accepted by the API, for example 5m, 300s, or 1h

  agr session get --space-id space-a1b2c3d4 --user-id user-123 --session-id session-123 -o text

  agr session event list --space-id space-a1b2c3d4 --user-id user-123 --session-id session-123 --offset 0 --limit 10 -o text

session.event.append.short: Append an event to a session
session.event.append.long: Append an interaction to an existing conversation. Keep the same SpaceId, UserId, and SessionId across turns. The event accepts inline JSON, @file, or - for stdin.
examples:
Example - Append a user event:
  agr session event append --space-id space-a1b2c3d4 --user-id user-123 --session-id session-123 --event '{"EventId":"event-123","Author":"user","Content":{"Role":"user","Parts":[{"Text":"Hello"}]}}' -o text

Example - Append a prepared event file:
  agr session event append --space-id space-a1b2c3d4 --user-id user-123 --session-id session-123 --event @event.json -o text

event.usage: Event content as a JSON object, @file, or - for stdin.
fields: EventId: optional event ID; the service generates one when it is empty
Author: event author
Content: structured event content
Actions: optional state delta
Metadata: optional event metadata JSON string
Extensions: optional extension JSON string

instance.snapshot.create.long:
Create a saved snapshot of an existing sandbox instance. The Runtime Snapshot API is Beta and may change incompatibly or be discontinued.

Provide --instance-id for a running instance with disk snapshot support enabled, and use --memory=false for a disk-only snapshot. When --memory is omitted, the CLI leaves Memory unset. The service defaults to including memory unless the source instance is configured for disk-only snapshots. Memory snapshots are currently unsupported.

Save the returned Snapshot.SnapshotId for list, restore, and delete operations. Once the snapshot is ACTIVE, restore it into a new instance with `agr instance create --snapshot-id <snapshot-id>`. Supply the same --client-token and request values when retrying an identical creation. The CLI does not automatically retry creation.
examples: agr instance snapshot create --instance-id ins-xxxx --memory=false --snapshot-name checkpoint --client-token snapshot-001 -o text

InstanceId.description: Source instance ID required by the service; must be running with disk snapshot support enabled.

instance-id.usage: Source instance ID required by the service; must be running with disk snapshot support enabled.

Memory.description: Use false for disk-only snapshots. Omission leaves Memory unset; true is currently unsupported.

memory.usage: Use false for disk-only snapshots. Omission leaves Memory unset; true is currently unsupported.

instance.snapshot.delete.long:
Request deletion of a saved sandbox snapshot. The Runtime Snapshot API is Beta and may change incompatibly or be discontinued.

Provide a snapshot ID as the positional argument or in --request. When stdin is a TTY, deletion requires confirmation and defaults to cancel. Use --yes (-y) to skip confirmation. With --non-interactive or non-TTY stdin, the request is sent without prompting. A successful response acknowledges deletion; cleanup can finish asynchronously. Inspect the snapshot with list to check its status.
examples: agr instance snapshot delete snapshot-xxxx -o text
agr instance snapshot delete snapshot-xxxx --yes -o text

SnapshotId.description: Snapshot ID to delete; provide the positional argument or SnapshotId in --request.

instance.snapshot.list.long:
List saved sandbox snapshots or query specific snapshot IDs. The Runtime Snapshot API is Beta and may change incompatibly or be discontinued.

Use --offset/--limit for offset pagination, or --max-results/--next-token for cursor pagination. Offset must be non-negative. Limit and MaxResults accept 0-100; 0 leaves that page-size option unset. If both page sizes are omitted or 0, the service uses 20. A nonempty NextToken conflicts with a positive Offset; positive MaxResults conflicts with positive Offset or Limit. Limit with NextToken is supported.

Pass a returned NextToken unchanged for the next page and keep SnapshotIds, Filters (including array order), and Limit unchanged. MaxResults may change between pages. The result includes SnapshotSet, TotalCount, and NextToken; an empty NextToken means there are no more pages. The CLI returns one page per invocation.
examples: agr instance snapshot list --snapshot-ids snapshot-xxxx -o text

SnapshotIds.description: Filter by snapshot IDs; repeat the flag for multiple IDs.

snapshot-ids.usage: Filter by snapshot IDs; repeat the flag for multiple IDs.

filters.usage: Filters as a JSON array, @file, or - for stdin.
fields: Name: filter name, for example status or snapshot-name
Values: filter values

Offset.description: Non-negative pagination offset; positive values conflict with a nonempty NextToken or positive MaxResults.

offset.usage: Non-negative pagination offset; positive values conflict with a nonempty NextToken or positive MaxResults.

Limit.description: Page size, 0-100; 0 or omission leaves it unset. Positive values conflict with positive MaxResults.

limit.usage: Page size, 0-100; 0 or omission leaves it unset. Positive values conflict with positive MaxResults.

NextToken.description: Cursor returned by the previous page; keep SnapshotIds, Filters (including array order), and Limit unchanged.

next-token.usage: Cursor returned by the previous page; keep SnapshotIds, Filters (including array order), and Limit unchanged.

MaxResults.description: Cursor page size, 0-100; 0 or omission leaves it unset. Positive values conflict with positive Offset or Limit.

max-results.usage: Cursor page size, 0-100; 0 or omission leaves it unset. Positive values conflict with positive Offset or Limit.
